diagnosis.root_cause: Marginal and oscillating optical RX signal on this customer's fibre path is causing repeated link/session interruptions. RX remains in the degraded band at the start and end of the seven-day window, repeatedly reaches critical levels, while TX power, TX bias, distance, ONU supply voltage, and peer ONUs remain healthy. The 16 sessions in 24 hours with short average duration confirm signal-driven flapping rather than normal re-authentication.
evidence: The ONU is currently online and responding, so this is not an ONU-offline event.
The customer's current RX power is -27.94 dBm, which is degraded and close to critical; TX power at 2.29 dBm is normal.

The seven-day RX series starts in the degraded band and ends in the degraded band, with repeated swings between approximately -24 and below -28 dBm. Per the discriminator, this is a marginal link oscillation rather than a declining trend.
Session activity is 16 in 24 hours, above the 8-session flapping threshold, and average duration is only 71 minutes versus the 11.9-hour network mean.
TX power is stable and TX bias current remains within the healthy range, so laser degradation is not indicated.
Distance is constant at 302 m, so there is no fibre-path or record distance step change.
Peers on EPON0/2 have healthy optical levels and all probed ONUs are online, ruling out a shared splitter, PON-port, or OLT fault.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, has normal CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime, and the router heartbeat is healthy.
RADIUS exists and matches CRM, the customer VLAN is correctly provisioned as 1092, and there is no authentication or VLAN inconsistency to explain the repeated sessions.
The evidence therefore identifies the customer's marginal optical fibre path as the cause of signal-driven session flapping.

remediation.action: Dispatch field maintenance to inspect and clean the ONU, drop fibre, connectors, splice points, and splitter connection; measure optical loss and locate intermittent attenuation or reflection. Repair or replace the affected fibre segment, connector, splice, or splitter leg as required. Continue monitoring RX stability and session count after repair.

ground_truth.root_cause: RX power oscillates between roughly -24.4 and -28.2 dBm on an eleven hour cycle, crossing the threshold at which the link stops being usable. The session drops follow the signal excursions.
expected_reasoning: Sixteen sessions in 24 hours against a 2-3 baseline, with a 71 minute mean duration
Cached RX is -26.28 dBm, already in the degraded band
Telemetry shows RX oscillating between about -24.4 and -28.2 dBm on an eleven hour cycle
The lower excursions cross -28 dBm, at which point the link becomes unusable
Live RX of -27.94 confirms the signal is currently near the bottom of that swing
TX power, bias current, supply voltage and distance are all stable, so the ONU is healthy
RADIUS is clean with a single consistent entry and no mismatches
Peers on EPON0/2 read normal, so the fault is in this customer's own path
The session pattern tracks the signal excursions, so the optical fault explains the flapping
distractors: The trigger names the session count, pointing at the auth layer
Sixteen disconnects is well within the observed flapping tail and could be read as a CPE fault
